text:
deploybot: Scheduled rollout for customer CopperCliff (Dedicated) tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. Canary slice: 3% traffic -> 20% at 10m -> 100% at 40m. Version pinned: v2.3.1-rc5. Please confirm pin and any blockers.
marie (eng-release): Acked the schedule. Docs PR is ready: https://git.internal/docs/coppercliff-rollout (diff + release notes).
sam (eng-sre): Quick note — KMS rotation for coppercliff service account is scheduled 01:30 UTC (prior to rollout). That collides if rotation fails. We should add a contingency.
alex (customer-success): Customer aware of 02:00 window; asked for no DB restart. They said they can tolerate 15min canary.
ben (ops): Can we avoid cache flush? KV cache will be preserved unless we change model shard. Confirming we won't change model id.
marie (eng-release): Confirmed: model id stays the same. Only runtime bump and quantization tweak. KV cache should survive.
natalie (product): What are our rollback triggers? Latency or correctness? Need concrete thresholds to notify customer.
sam (eng-sre): Propose: immediate rollback if 95th latency increases >30% for canary AND error rate >1%. If latency alone spikes but error stable, hold at canary and triage for 10 mins.
ben (ops): Agree. Add token-generation regression monitor: if avg tokens/s drops >25% for canary requests -> pause ramp.
marie (eng-release): Adding the rollback commands here for on-call ops:
```
# rollback to previous stable
redwoodctl rollout set --customer coppercliff --version v2.3.0-stable --reason "canary rollback"
# emergency drain
redwoodctl route set --customer coppercliff --slice canary --weight 0
```
sam (eng-sre): I'll wire up alerts: pager if error rate >1% or 95th latency +30% for 2 consecutive 1m buckets. Also dashboard link: https://metrics.internal/d/coppercliff/rollout-canary
alex (customer-success): Customer asked for a post-rollout note with exact timing and whether any PII touched. prod, keep that in mind.
marie (eng-release): Release notes section: "runtime optimized; quantization profile Q4; no model changes; expected token-cost -7%" — added.
natalie (product): Is the canary window shortened to 15m per customer ask? We said 10m->40m previously. Propose 15m -> 45m full ramp if green. Opinions?
ben (ops): 15m canary is fine but keep the slow ramp steps: 3% -> 15% at 15m -> 50% at 30m -> 100% at 60m. Safer for KV cache warmup.
marie (eng-release): Updated plan in PR. Also tagging release-engineer on-call @sam for rollback runbook.
sam (eng-sre): Acknowledged. I'll be on primary pager 01:45-03:15 UTC.
deploybot: deploybot started canary slice at 02:00:00 UTC — slice id canary-cc-03.
ben (ops): Seeing normal request rates to canary slice. KV cache warmup looks steady.
natalie (product): Customer ops team in the thread — they said they saw 1xxs but nothing critical yet.
marie (eng-release): Ramp to 15% at 02:15.
sam (eng-sre): Metrics: 95th latency +8%, error rate 0.2% — within thresholds. Holding 15m.
marie (eng-release): Ramp to 50% at 02:30.
ben (ops): Observability note: token/sec down 5% during first 10m then stabilized. No action.
alex (customer-success): Customer confirms no DB restarts observed. They appreciate the heads-up.
marie (eng-release): Ramp to 100% at 03:00.
sam (eng-sre): Post-rollout checks passing. Marking rollout successful.
alex (customer-success): Customer happy. Sending post-rollout summary now.
marie (eng-release): Closing thread. Docs PR merged and release notes published. :tada:
